Methylboronic acid-derived linear polyborosiloxanes with fluorinated side-chain regulation for stable Si–O–B dynamic silicone elastomers
Synthesis and Comparative Study of Polysiloxane Networks Cross‐Linked by Di‐ and Trivalent Metal Ions
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    A series of metal‐containing polysiloxane networks were synthesized using dibenzoylmethane‐functionalized precursors and various divalent (Mg
                     2+ 
                    , Zn
                     2+ 
                    , Cu
                     2+ 
                    ) and trivalent (Fe
                     3+ 
                    , Mn
                     3+ 
                    , Eu
                     3+ 
                    ) metal acetates. It was found that the use of trivalent metal ions significantly enhances the mechanical integrity of the materials, driving a transition from weak, gel‐like substances (divalent systems) to self‐standing, flexible films. Notably, the Mn
                     3+ 
                    ‐cross‐linked polymer exhibited a remarkable elongation at break of up to 863%, suggesting a highly dynamic coordination environment. Thermal analysis (TGA/DSC) indicated that the polymers are stable up to 300°C and demonstrate a glass transition temperature near −120°C. Furthermore, the incorporation of Eu
                     3+ 
                    ions provided the films with characteristic red photoluminescence. These results demonstrate that metal cross‐linking is an effective strategy for developing functional, highly elastic, and thermostable siloxane‐based materials.
source: Wiley - Journal of Applied Polymer Science

title: Room Temperature Self‐Healable Thermoplastic‐Elastomeric Blend Materials Based on Reversible Imine Bonded Cross‐Linked Polydimethylsiloxane Elastomer and Thermoplastic Polyurethane in Association With H‐Bonding and Their Characterization
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   Herein, both reversible covalent bonds (imine bond) and noncovalent interactions (H‐bonding) are incorporated into thermoplastic elastomeric blend materials to impart remarkable self‐healing properties at room temperature without any external stimuli. First, a Schiff base reaction occurs between amino‐functionalized polydimethylsiloxane (AFPDMS) and 1, 3, 5‐triformylbenzene (TFB), generating reversible imine‐bonded polydimethylsiloxane elastomer (CL‐PDMS), which is usually mechanically weak. Hence, thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) is blended with it to obtain a blend material having good mechanical properties as well as room temperature healing ability. FTIR analysis confirmed both the presence of imine bonds in CL‐PDMS and hydrogen bonding between CL‐PDMS and TPU. The healing efficiency is dependent on the healing time and TFB content. Additionally, as the content of TPU in the blend increased, the healing efficiency and tensile properties correspondingly increased. The tensile strength of 200.7 kPa and elongation at break of 155.6% was observed for the CL‐PDMS/TPU (80/20) wt.% blend sample. This blend exhibited a maximum healing efficiency and recovered 98.7% and 96.4% of its original tensile strength and elongation‐at‐break, respectively, when healed at room temperature for 6 h. Moreover, graphene oxide was integrated with this polymer blend system to prepare self‐healing materials that may be used for flexible electronic devices.
source: Wiley - Journal of Applied Polymer Science

title:
Fabrication of a Polysiloxane Incorporating Hybrid Units With an Increased Ratio of
                     N 
                    ‐Halamine to Quaternary Ammonium Salt on Cellulose: A General Tactic for Better Antibacterial Synergism
summary:
ABSTRACT 
                   
                    The adjustment of the ratio of synergistic components in a hybrid unit of a polymer is demonstrated as a strategy for even better biocidability. Briefly, an
                     N 
                    ‐halamine precursor, 1‐(3‐hydroxypropyl)‐1,3,5‐triazinane‐2,4,6‐trione, was synthesized through nucleophilic substitution between 1,3,5‐triazinane‐2,4,6‐trione and 3‐chloro‐1‐propanol. Itaconic anhydride was then used to bridge 2‐(dimethylamino)ethan‐1‐ol and the precursor via alcoholysis and esterification. The tertiary amine and CC bond of the esterification compound underwent reactions with 1‐chlorohexane and trimethoxysilane through quaternization and hydrosilylation, respectively. The molecules of the hydrosilylation compound were hydrolyzed and then crosslinked into a polysiloxane layer with pendants of one quaternary ammonium salt and two NH bonds on cellulose via dehydrocondensation. Following chlorination of the NH bonds to NCl counterparts, the cellulose was coated with a 96 nm layer containing the target hybrid units. Time‐kill assessments revealed that the quaternary ammonium salt and
                     N 
                    ‐halamine structures functioned synergistically, resulting in greater efficacy than a previously reported 1:1 combination and hence demonstrating a better antibacterial synergism. Antibacterial durability and rechargeability on cellulose were both encouraging owing to the robust three‐dimensional crosslinked polysiloxane and the stable cyclic
                     N 
                    ‐halamine. This study proposes a tactic for better antibacterial synergism through the increase of the proportion of
                     N 
                    ‐halamine in a hybrid unit.
source: Wiley - Journal of Applied Polymer Science
